Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
908 AM PST Fri Nov 27 2026

.SYNOPSIS...27/257 AM.

Warm temperatures and dry weather is expected through Satuday due
to a predominant offshore flow pattern. Temperatures will peak 
today with some gusty northeast winds at times, then cooling will
begin over the weekend. There is a high possibility of a large 
storm system around the middle of next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SUN)...27/907 AM.

***UPDATE***

Offshore pressure gradients are beginning to weaken as surface 
pressures fall to the north in response to approaching storms.
There are still some lingering Santa Ana winds in a few areas but
overall winds are on the decrease. The main thing on Black Friday  
is the very warm weather with highs again in the 80s in many
coast/valley areas, around 15 degrees above normal. Temperature
records are mostly out of reach but a few areas could come within
a couple degrees of records. 

***From Previous Discussion***

A large east pac ridge nosing in from the SW will dominate the
weather today and Saturday. Offshore flow will continue today
although weaker than it was on Thanksgiving Day. By Saturday there
will only be very weak offshore or neutral flow in the morning
turning onshore in the afternoon. Skies will be mostly clear. Max
temps will be similar to ydy today with lower to mid 80s across 
the csts/vlys of VTA/LA counties and in the mid to upper 70s 
across the csts/vlys of SLO/SBA counties. The return to onshore
flow on Saturday will bring 3 to 6 degrees of cooling to most
areas. Even with the cooling max temps will end up 3 to 6 degrees
above normal.

The ridge pushes to the east Saturday night and on Sunday broad
westerly slightly difluent flow will be overhead. There will be
plenty of clouds embedded in the flow and it will be a mostly
cloudy day. A weak impulse will move through with the flow and
will bring a chc of light rain (under a tenth) to the Central
Coast in the afternoon. Rain is likely (70 percent chc) for the
Central Coast in the evening with a 30-40 percent chc of light
rain south of Pt Conception. Areas north of Morro Bay may see a
quarter inch of rain, but all other areas will see, at most, a
tenth and likely much less.

Onshore flow, lower hgts, and plenty of clouds will all combine to
lower max temps by 4 to 8 degrees which will bring them down to
normal levels.

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...27/257 AM.

On Monday the area will cover by broad moist difluent flow ahead
of a storm system to the west. Periods of on again off again rain
is likely through the day. Rainfall amounts will likely amount to
between a quarter and a third of an inch for the csts/vlys and
coastal slopes. Much less rain will fall across the far interior.
Max temps will collapse into the mid 60s to lower 70s.

Near 100 percent chc of moderate to strong storm in the Monday
night to early Wednesday time frame. An 548 dam upper low is 
forecast to approach and swing over the area during this time 
frame. PWATs with the storm will be near 1.2 inches which is about
8 tenths of an inch greater than normal. The fact the cold upper
low is passing overhead combined with the anomalously warm ocean
temps means that this storm will have an enhanced convective
potential. Still too early to resolve the finer details and timing
of this system but it is going to be one to watch. The rainfall
total forecast remains consistent at 1 to 3 inches for the csts
and vlys and 3 to 5 inches for the coastal slopes and foothills.
There is also a greater than normal chc of strong winds (50+ mph
gusts). This storm is entraining subtropical moisture and that
means it will be warmer system with snow levels at or above 7500
ft. Highs will be in the mid 60s for most of the csts/vlys both
days.

A little ridge will bring dry conditions to the area on Thursday
with a weak likely inconsequential system still slated for 
Friday.

&&

.AVIATION...27/1056Z.

At 0827Z at KLAX, there was a surface-based inversion. The top of
the inversion was at 1500 feet with a temp of 20 deg C.

High confidence in VFR TAFs.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Good confidence that any east 
wind component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...27/833 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Expecting Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas with 
areas of SCA level winds to persist through tonight. Then conds 
will be largely below SCA levels Saturday through Monday before 
winds increase Monday evening to SCA levels ahead of an 
approaching strong storm system. Winds are expected to increase 
further to Gale Force late Monday night and continue through 
Tuesday night along with large and increasingly hazardous seas as 
the storm impacts the area.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Expecting SCA level seas lasting 
through this evening. Conds will be largely below SCA levels 
Saturday through Monday before winds increase Monday evening to 
SCA levels ahead of an approaching strong storm system. Winds are 
expected to increase further to Gale Force late Monday night and 
continue through Tuesday night along with large and increasingly 
hazardous seas as the storm impacts the area.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Today through Monday, winds and 
seas are expected to remain below SCA. Winds are expected to 
increase to SCA to Gale Force levels Monday night ahead of an 
approaching strong storm system. Gale Force winds are expected 
Tuesday and Tuesday night as the storm impacts the region.

&&

.BEACHES...27/833 AM.

A large, long period, west swell will continue to slowly subside
across the waters. Exceptionally high tides of 7.4 to 7.7 feet 
are expected this morning and up to 7.2 feet Saturday morning, and
this will continue the threat of moderate coastal flooding over 
low-lying coastal areas. A Coastal Flood Advisory continues until 
4 PM today for many beaches and until 2 PM Saturday for the 
Ventura County beaches.

High surf with the moderate coastal flooding issues this morning 
are expected across the Central Coast from Point Conception 
northward, as well as the Ventura County and Los Angeles County 
coastlines. Elsewhere, there may still be minor coastal flooding 
issues. Moderate coastal flooding will continue to be an issue 
Saturday morning for the Ventura County coastline during the late 
morning high tide. 

Low-lying coastal areas with no protection from the ocean will be
most vulnerable to sea water intrusion. There will be many, 
strong rip currently nearly everywhere, strong long shore 
currents, some risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, and 
coastal erosion. These conditions will lead to an increased risk 
of drowning and make swimming dangerous.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories in effect.
